applies_why: The judge text grounds an UNDERDETERMINED label on a single verse admitting two readings, which is what K-S2 addresses.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: The phrase "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open": I weighed whether admitting both readings makes the verse open/UNDERDETERMINED, or whether both senses stand and the verse is not open.
why: K-S2 says a verse carrying two senses is not open and both senses stand, but the judge text instead treats the two admitted readings of Matthew 1:16 as a reason for UNDERDETERMINED.
